executive_delta.template: PPI year-on-year eased to {obs:cn_ppi_yoy@2026-07} from {obs:cn_ppi_yoy@2026-06}, and the month-on-month print turned more negative at {obs:cn_ppi_mom@2026-07}.

The three-month average of PPI month-on-month momentum is now {drv:ma(cn_ppi_mom,3)@2026-07}, against {drv:ma(cn_ppi_mom,3)@2026-06} a month earlier, which flipped {test:T-H1-01} against the price-turn hypothesis.

Headline CPI slowed to {obs:cn_cpi_yoy@2026-07} from {obs:cn_cpi_yoy@2026-06} while core CPI was little changed at {obs:cn_core_cpi_yoy@2026-07}; the flip in {test:T-H2-01} rests on a six-month change of only {drv:diff(cn_core_cpi_yoy,6)@2026-07}.
Consumer-goods PPI is still negative at {obs:cn_ppi_consumer_yoy@2026-07}, barely different from {obs:cn_ppi_consumer_yoy@2026-06}, so the producer-goods strength has not passed downstream.

hypothesis_impact.divergence_reason: No H0 test flipped, but fading month-on-month momentum with consumer-goods prices still negative is the pattern an upstream-led bounce would show as it runs out.
hypothesis_impact.rationale_template: {test:T-H0-03} still holds with consumer-goods PPI at {obs:cn_ppi_consumer_yoy@2026-07}, while momentum faded.
Momentum is the weak leg of the price turn: {test:T-H1-01} flipped to challenging while the year-on-year level, now {obs:cn_ppi_yoy@2026-07}, is still high.

hypothesis_impact.divergence_reason: The only supporting flip, {test:T-H2-01}, rests on a six-month core CPI change of {drv:diff(cn_core_cpi_yoy,6)@2026-07} while the latest core print changed by {drv:diff(cn_core_cpi_yoy,1)@2026-07}: that is within noise, not a broadening of demand.
hypothesis_impact.rationale_template: The rule reads supportive, but the margin behind it is {drv:diff(cn_core_cpi_yoy,6)@2026-07} and the latest month moved the other way.

preliminary_implications.template: If momentum stays negative while consumer-goods PPI stays near {obs:cn_ppi_consumer_yoy@2026-07}, the upstream-led reading gains over a demand-led one.
